source.text: וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הָאָשָׁ֑ם קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is the] law of the guilt offering: a holy of holy things it [is].

en.L: And this [is] the law of the guilt offering: it [is] a most holy [thing].
en.B: These are the instructions for the guilt offering. It is most holy.
en.R: Here are the rules for the guilt offering. It is very holy.

decisions.choice: the law of the guilt offering: the priests' rules for the offering of 5:14-26
decisions.reason: Chapter 5 told the worshiper when a guilt offering is owed: for misusing holy things (5:15) or for wronging a neighbor (5:21-24), with the value of the loss repaid and a fifth added. It said nothing about how the animal is offered. Verses 1-7 now give the priests that procedure, step by step, as 4:1-5:13 and 6:18-23 did for the sin offering. The guilt offering repairs a wrong; on this sense of the word see 5:15.

decisions.choice: most holy: as in 6:10 and 6:18
decisions.reason: Like the sin offering, the guilt offering may be eaten only by the male priests, in the holy place (verse 6).

decisions.choice: and this: the speech of 6:18 continues
decisions.reason: The speech that began at 6:17-18 runs on through this chapter to verse 21. The guilt offering follows the sin offering in the same address to Aaron and his sons.

source.text: בִּמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁחֲטוּ֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֹלָ֔ה יִשְׁחֲט֖וּ אֶת־הָאָשָׁ֑ם וְאֶת־דָּמ֛וֹ יִזְרֹ֥ק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] place where they slaughter the burnt offering they will slaughter the guilt offering, and its blood he will throw on the altar all around.

en.L: In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering they shall slaughter the guilt offering, and its blood he shall throw on the altar all around.
en.B: The guilt offering is to be slaughtered at the same place as the burnt offering, and the priest is to splash its blood all around on the altar.
en.R: Kill the animal for the guilt offering at the place where the burnt offerings are killed. The priest must splash its blood on every side of the altar.

decisions.choice: the place where they slaughter the burnt offering: north of the altar
decisions.reason: The burnt offering is killed "on the north side of the altar" (1:11), and the sin offering in the same place (6:18).

decisions.choice: throw its blood on the altar all around: as for the burnt and peace offerings
decisions.reason: The blood is thrown against the sides of the altar, as with the burnt offering (1:5) and the peace offering (3:2). It is not put on the horns of the altar, as the blood of the sin offering is (4:25, 30).

decisions.choice: the priest
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he will throw". The one who handles the blood is the priest (1:5), so Balanced and Readable name him.

decisions.choice: kill
decisions.reason: Readable says "kill" for the verb for slaughtering an animal in sacrifice, as in 6:18.

source.text: וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־חֶלְבּ֖וֹ יַקְרִ֣יב מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֵ֚ת הָֽאַלְיָ֔ה וְאֶת־הַחֵ֖לֶב הַֽמְכַסֶּ֥ה אֶת־הַקֶּֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And all its fat he will present from it, the fat tail and the fat [which] covers the entrails,

en.L: And all its fat he shall bring near from it: the fat tail, and the fat that covers the entrails,
en.B: All its fat is to be offered from it: the fat tail, the fat that covers the internal organs,
en.R: The priest must offer all of its fat. That means the fat tail, the fat that covers the insides,

decisions.choice: the fat tail: the broad tail of a sheep
decisions.reason: The guilt offering is a ram (5:15, 25), and the sheep of the region had a broad tail heavy with fat. It is offered with the other fat parts, as in the peace offering of a sheep (3:9).

decisions.choice: all its fat: the same parts as in the peace and sin offerings
decisions.reason: The list in verses 3-4 is the one given for the peace offering (3:9-10) and the sin offering (4:8-9). On the fat as the LORD's portion see 3:3 and 3:16-17.

decisions.choice: The priest
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he will present". Readable names the priest, who burns the fat on the altar (verse 5).

source.text: וְאֵת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י הַכְּלָיֹ֔ת וְאֶת־הַחֵ֨לֶב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַכְּסָלִ֑ים וְאֶת־הַיֹּתֶ֨רֶת֙ עַל־הַכָּבֵ֔ד עַל־הַכְּלָיֹ֖ת יְסִירֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: and the two kidneys and the fat which [is] on them, which [is] on the loins, and the lobe on the liver; with the kidneys he will remove it.

en.L: and the two kidneys and the fat that [is] on them, which [is] on the loins, and the appendage on the liver; with the kidneys he shall remove it.
en.B: the two kidneys with the fat on them by the lower back, and the long lobe of the liver, which is to be taken out together with the kidneys.
en.R: both kidneys with the fat on them near the lower back, and the best part of the liver. He must take that part out along with the kidneys.

decisions.choice: the appendage on the liver: as in 3:4
decisions.reason: The same organ as in the peace offering; see the note on 3:4.

decisions.choice: with the kidneys he will remove it: the lobe is taken out with the kidneys
decisions.reason: As in 3:4, the lobe of the liver is removed together with the kidneys and their fat.

decisions.choice: the lower back
decisions.reason: "Loins" means the area of the back below the ribs, where the kidneys lie. Balanced and Readable say "the lower back", as in 3:4.

source.text: וְהִקְטִ֨יר אֹתָ֤ם הַכֹּהֵן֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה אָשָׁ֖ם הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And the priest will make them smoke on the altar, a fire offering to Yahweh; a guilt offering it [is].

en.L: And the priest shall make them smoke on the altar, an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it [is] a guilt offering.
en.B: The priest is to turn them into smoke on the altar as a food offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is a guilt offering.
en.R: The priest must burn these parts on the altar. They are a food offering burned on the altar for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is a guilt offering.

decisions.choice: make smoke ... a fire offering: as in 1:9
decisions.reason: The fat parts go up in smoke to God as his portion. See 1:9 on both terms.

decisions.choice: a guilt offering it is: a closing formula
decisions.reason: The short statement names the kind of offering, as "it is a burnt offering" does in 1:9 and "it is a sin offering" in 4:21. It marks the end of the altar rite.

source.text: כָּל־זָכָ֥ר בַּכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יֹאכְלֶ֑נּוּ בְּמָק֤וֹם קָדוֹשׁ֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: Every male among [the] priests will eat it; in a place holy it will be eaten; a holy of holy things it [is].

en.L: Every male among the priests shall eat it; in a holy place it shall be eaten; it [is] a most holy [thing].
en.B: Any male of priestly descent may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
en.R: Any male in the priests' families may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is very holy.

decisions.choice: every male among the priests: as in 6:22
decisions.reason: The meat may be shared among the males of the priestly families, as with the sin offering (6:22) and the grain offering (6:11).

decisions.choice: in a holy place: the courtyard of the tent of meeting
decisions.reason: As in 6:9 and 6:19, the most holy offerings are eaten inside the courtyard, not taken home.

source.text: כַּֽחַטָּאת֙ כָּֽאָשָׁ֔ם תּוֹרָ֥ה אַחַ֖ת לָהֶ֑ם הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְכַפֶּר־בּ֖וֹ ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: As the sin offering, as the guilt offering; one law [is] to them; the priest who makes atonement with it, to him it will belong.

en.L: As the sin offering, so the guilt offering; one law [is] for them: the priest who makes atonement with it, it shall belong to him.
en.B: The guilt offering is like the sin offering: the same rule applies to both. The animal belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
en.R: The guilt offering is like the sin offering. The same rule is true for both. The meat belongs to the priest who uses it to make atonement.

decisions.choice: one law for them: the rule about who receives the meat
decisions.reason: The two offerings differ in how the blood is used (verse 2; 4:25), so the shared rule is the one the verse goes on to state: the meat goes to the officiating priest, as with the sin offering (6:19).

decisions.choice: makes atonement: as in 1:4
decisions.reason: The guilt offering, like the sin offering, makes atonement for the one who brings it (5:16, 18, 26).

decisions.choice: the same rule (Balanced); The same rule (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in "the law of the guilt offering" (verse 1), here meaning a single rule that covers both offerings. Literal keeps "one law".

decisions.choice: The animal (Balanced); The meat (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "it". What the priest receives is the meat of the offering, as verse 6 implies.

source.text: וְהַ֨כֹּהֵ֔ן הַמַּקְרִ֖יב אֶת־עֹ֣לַת אִ֑ישׁ ע֤וֹר הָֽעֹלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְרִ֔יב לַכֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the priest [who] presents a burnt offering of anyone, the hide of the burnt offering which he presented, to the priest to him it will belong.

en.L: And the priest who brings near {{gender:anyone's|a man's}} burnt offering, the hide of the burnt offering that he brought near shall belong to the priest; it shall be his.
en.B: When a priest offers a burnt offering for {{gender:someone|a man}}, the hide of the animal he offered is his to keep.
en.R: When a priest offers a burnt offering for {{gender:someone|a man}}, the skin of that animal belongs to the priest.

decisions.choice: the hide of the burnt offering: the one part not burned
decisions.reason: The burnt offering is skinned before it is cut up (1:6), and everything else goes up in smoke (1:9). The hide, of real value for leather, is the priest's payment for his service.

decisions.choice: anyone: any worshiper, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word usually means "a man", but in laws like this one it means "anyone, each". A woman could also bring a burnt offering (12:6).

decisions.choice: anyone's / someone (default); a man's / a man (alternative)
decisions.reason: The rule applies to whoever brings the offering, so the default is inclusive and the word-for-word "a man" is the alternative.

source.text: וְכָל־מִנְחָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר תֵּֽאָפֶה֙ בַּתַּנּ֔וּר וְכָל־נַעֲשָׂ֥ה בַמַּרְחֶ֖שֶׁת וְעַֽל־מַחֲבַ֑ת לַכֹּהֵ֛ן הַמַּקְרִ֥יב אֹתָ֖הּ ל֥וֹ תִֽהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And every grain offering which is baked in the oven, and all [that] has been made in the pan and on a baking tray, to the priest [who] presents it, to him it will belong.

en.L: And every grain offering that is baked in the oven, and all that is made in the pan or on a griddle, shall belong to the priest who brings it near; it shall be his.
en.B: Any grain offering that has been baked in an oven, or prepared in a pan or on a griddle, is to go to the priest who presents it.
en.R: A grain offering may be baked in an oven or cooked in a deep pan or on a flat pan. Then it belongs to the priest who offers it.

decisions.choice: baked in the oven, made in the pan or on a griddle: the cooked grain offerings of 2:4-7
decisions.reason: Chapter 2 lists grain offerings baked in an oven (2:4), cooked on a flat griddle (2:5) and cooked in a pan (2:7). After the memorial portion is burned (2:9), the rest goes to the priest who offers it.

decisions.choice: to the priest who presents it: the officiating priest alone
decisions.reason: Cooked grain offerings go to the priest who serves, in contrast with the uncooked ones, which all the priests share (verse 10).

decisions.choice: or
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the last two items with "and", meaning either of them. Literal says "or" so that the list does not suggest one offering made in both.

decisions.choice: a deep pan ... a flat pan
decisions.reason: Readable describes the two cooking vessels of 2:5 and 2:7 by their shape, as in 6:14.

source.text: וְכָל־מִנְחָ֥ה בְלוּלָֽה־בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן וַחֲרֵבָ֑ה לְכָל־בְּנֵ֧י אַהֲרֹ֛ן תִּהְיֶ֖ה אִ֥ישׁ כְּאָחִֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And every grain offering mixed with oil and dry, to all the sons of Aaron it will belong, each like his brother.

en.L: And every grain offering mixed with oil or dry shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, each one like his brother.
en.B: Every other grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all of Aaron's sons, to be shared alike among them.
en.R: Other grain offerings are not cooked. They may be mixed with oil or be dry. All of Aaron's sons must share these equally.

decisions.choice: mixed with oil or dry: uncooked grain offerings
decisions.reason: These are the offerings of flour not baked or cooked: fine flour with oil (2:1-3) and the dry flour of the poor person's sin offering, which has no oil (5:11). The verse sets them against the cooked offerings of verse 9.

decisions.choice: each like his brother: in equal shares
decisions.reason: The phrase means that every priest receives the same share as another.

decisions.choice: Other grain offerings are not cooked.
decisions.reason: Readable states the contrast with verse 9 that the verse implies: these offerings are raw flour.

source.text: וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת זֶ֣בַח הַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַקְרִ֖יב לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is the] law of the sacrifice of the peace offerings which someone will present to Yahweh.

en.L: And this [is] the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings that one brings near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: These are the instructions for the peace offering that someone brings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Here are the rules for the peace offering that a person brings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings: the rules for eating the offering of chapter 3
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 gave the altar rite for the peace offering. These verses (11-36) tell who eats the meat, and when. Unlike the offerings of 6:1-7:10, most of the peace offering is eaten by the worshiper. Verses 12-18 name three kinds: for thanksgiving, for a vow, and freely given.

decisions.choice: which someone will present: any worshiper
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It means whoever brings such an offering.

source.text: אִ֣ם עַל־תּוֹדָה֮ יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ֒ וְהִקְרִ֣יב׀עַל־זֶ֣בַח הַתּוֹדָ֗ה חַלּ֤וֹת מַצּוֹת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וּרְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּשָּׁ֑מֶן וְסֹ֣לֶת מֻרְבֶּ֔כֶת חַלֹּ֖ת בְּלוּלֹ֥ת בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: If on thanksgiving he will present it, and he will present with the sacrifice of the thanksgiving cakes of unleavened bread mixed with oil, and wafers of unleavened bread smeared with oil, and fine flour well mixed, cakes mixed with oil.

en.L: If he brings it near for thanksgiving, then he shall bring near with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil, and fine flour well soaked, cakes mixed with oil.
en.B: If it is brought to give thanks, the worshiper must also present, with the thanksgiving sacrifice, loaves made without yeast and mixed with oil, wafers made without yeast and spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour well soaked and mixed with oil.
en.R: Someone may bring a peace offering to give thanks. Then they must also bring bread made without yeast: thick loaves mixed with oil, thin wafers brushed with oil, and loaves of fine flour soaked through with oil.

decisions.choice: thanksgiving: an offering given to thank and praise God for what he has done
decisions.reason: The word means both thanks and the open acknowledgment of what God has done. A person who had been rescued from danger, sickness or trouble brought this offering and told of God's help before others (Psalm 107:21-22; 116:12-19; Jonah 2:9). Thanksgiving was sung as well as sacrificed (Psalm 50:14, 23; Jeremiah 33:11). It is the first of three kinds of peace offering: given in thanks, to keep a vow, or freely (verse 16).

decisions.choice: cakes, wafers and soaked loaves: bread eaten with the meat
decisions.reason: A thanksgiving was a meal, and the bread was eaten with the meat. The three kinds are those of the grain offerings baked in an oven (2:4) and the bread of the ordination (8:26). One of each is given to the priest (verse 14).

decisions.choice: well mixed: soaked through with oil
decisions.reason: The same word as in 6:14, used of dough worked with oil until it is saturated.

decisions.choice: the worshiper (Balanced); they (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he" for the one who brings the offering, a man or a woman. Literal keeps "he"; Balanced says "the worshiper" and Readable "they", as in 1:2.

decisions.choice: thanksgiving sacrifice (Balanced); a peace offering to give thanks (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the offering "the thanksgiving sacrifice"; Readable says what it is for.

source.text: עַל־חַלֹּת֙ לֶ֣חֶם חָמֵ֔ץ יַקְרִ֖יב קָרְבָּנ֑וֹ עַל־זֶ֖בַח תּוֹדַ֥ת שְׁלָמָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: With cakes of bread of leaven he will present his present, with the sacrifice of the thanksgiving of his peace offerings.

en.L: With cakes of leavened bread he shall bring near his offering, with the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offerings.
en.B: With their thanksgiving peace offering they are also to present loaves of bread made with yeast.
en.R: They must also bring loaves of bread made with yeast along with their peace offering of thanks.

decisions.choice: cakes of leavened bread: bread for the meal, not for the altar
decisions.reason: Nothing made with leaven may be burned on the altar (2:11). This bread is not burned: one loaf goes to the priest (verse 14) and the rest is eaten with the meat. Leavened loaves are presented also at the Festival of Weeks (23:17).

decisions.choice: the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offerings: a thanksgiving is a kind of peace offering
decisions.reason: The phrase joins the two names: the thanksgiving is one form of the peace offering, so the rules of chapter 3 apply to its altar rite.

decisions.choice: they ... their
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, Balanced and Readable use "they" for the worshiper, who may be a man or a woman. Literal keeps "he".

source.text: וְהִקְרִ֨יב מִמֶּ֤נּוּ אֶחָד֙ מִכָּל־קָרְבָּ֔ן תְּרוּמָ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה לַכֹּהֵ֗ן הַזֹּרֵ֛ק אֶת־דַּ֥ם הַשְּׁלָמִ֖ים ל֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will present from it one [loaf] from every present [as] a contribution to Yahweh; to the priest [who] sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings, to him it will belong.

en.L: And he shall bring near from it one from each offering [as] a contribution to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; to the priest who throws the blood of the peace offerings, it shall belong to him.
en.B: From each kind of offering they are to present one loaf as a contribution to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offering.
en.R: From each kind of bread they must give one loaf as a gift set apart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That loaf belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offering.

decisions.choice: one from every offering: one piece of each kind of bread
decisions.reason: The worshiper sets aside one loaf or wafer of each kind named in verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: a contribution: a portion set apart for God and given to the priest
decisions.reason: See the note on verse 32. What is set apart "to the LORD" becomes the priest's.

decisions.choice: the priest who throws the blood: the officiating priest
decisions.reason: The priest who performs the blood rite (3:2) receives the bread, as he receives the right thigh (verse 33).

decisions.choice: one loaf
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "one". The context shows that a loaf or wafer is meant.

source.text: וּבְשַׂ֗ר זֶ֚בַח תּוֹדַ֣ת שְׁלָמָ֔יו בְּי֥וֹם קָרְבָּנ֖וֹ יֵאָכֵ֑ל לֹֽא־יַנִּ֥יחַ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the meat of the sacrifice of the thanksgiving of his peace offerings on the day of his present it will be eaten; not he will leave any of it until morning.

en.L: And the flesh of the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offerings shall be eaten on the day of his offering; he shall not leave any of it until morning.
en.B: The meat of the peace offering given in thanks is to be eaten the same day it is offered. Nothing of it is to be kept until the next morning.
en.R: The meat of the thank offering must be eaten on the same day it is offered. Do not keep any of it until the next morning.

decisions.choice: on the day of his offering ... not until morning: one day only
decisions.reason: The meat of a thanksgiving must be finished the same day, as with the Passover lamb (Exodus 12:10) and the ordination ram (Exodus 29:34). The vow and freewill offerings allow two days (verse 16). What remains is burned (compare 7:17).

decisions.choice: he will not leave: the worshiper and those who share the meal
decisions.reason: The worshiper is responsible for seeing that the meal is eaten in the time allowed. The meal could be shared with family and guests who were clean (verse 19).

decisions.choice: Nothing of it is to be kept (Balanced); Do not keep (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a passive and Readable speaks to the reader, so that neither needs "he" for a worshiper who may be a man or a woman.

source.text: וְאִם־נֶ֣דֶר׀א֣וֹ נְדָבָ֗ה זֶ֚בַח קָרְבָּנ֔וֹ בְּי֛וֹם הַקְרִיב֥וֹ אֶת־זִבְח֖וֹ יֵאָכֵ֑ל וּמִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וְהַנּוֹתָ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ יֵאָכֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And if [is] a vow or a freewill offering the sacrifice of his present, on the day he presents his sacrifice it will be eaten, and from [the] next day the remainder of it will be eaten.

en.L: And if the sacrifice of his offering [is] a vow or a freewill offering, on the day he brings near his sacrifice it shall be eaten, and on the next day what remains of it may be eaten.
en.B: If the sacrifice is offered to fulfill a vow, or as a freewill offering, it is to be eaten on the day it is presented, and the rest may still be eaten the following day.
en.R: Someone may bring a peace offering to keep a promise they made to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or simply because they want to give it. Then the meat may be eaten on the day it is offered. What is left may also be eaten the next day.

decisions.choice: a vow: an offering promised to God and now paid
decisions.reason: A vow is a solemn promise to give God something, often made in a time of need and paid when the prayer has been answered (Genesis 28:20-22; 1 Samuel 1:11, 24-28; Psalm 66:13-14). Once made, it must be kept (Deuteronomy 23:21-23; Ecclesiastes 5:4-5). The peace offering is one way of paying it (22:21; Numbers 15:8). Chapter 27 deals with vows of persons and property.

decisions.choice: a freewill offering: given of one's own accord
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to be willing or moved to give. It is not owed for any sin and not promised in advance: the worshiper simply chooses to give it (22:18, 21, 23; Exodus 35:29; Deuteronomy 16:10). Lesser animals were acceptable for it than for a vow (22:23).

decisions.choice: on the next day: two days for these offerings
decisions.reason: The thanksgiving must be eaten on the day it is offered (verse 15); the vow and freewill offerings may be eaten over two days. The meat must not reach the third day (verses 17-18).

decisions.choice: to keep a promise they made to the LORD, or simply because they want to give it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two terms by what each offering is for.

source.text: וְהַנּוֹתָ֖ר מִבְּשַׂ֣ר הַזָּ֑בַח בַּיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י בָּאֵ֖שׁ יִשָּׂרֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And the remainder of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day with fire it will be burned.

en.L: And what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned with fire.
en.B: But any meat from the sacrifice still left on the third day must be burned up.
en.R: Any meat still left on the third day must be burned up.

decisions.choice: burned: destroyed by fire
decisions.reason: This is the ordinary verb for burning, as in 6:23, not the verb for making an offering smoke on the altar. The leftover meat is destroyed so that it cannot be eaten (19:6).

source.text: וְאִ֣ם הֵאָכֹ֣ל יֵ֠אָכֵל מִבְּשַׂר־זֶ֨בַח שְׁלָמָ֜יו בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֮ לֹ֣א יֵרָצֶה֒ הַמַּקְרִ֣יב אֹת֗וֹ לֹ֧א יֵחָשֵׁ֛ב ל֖וֹ פִּגּ֣וּל יִהְיֶ֑ה וְהַנֶּ֛פֶשׁ הָאֹכֶ֥לֶת מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עֲוֺנָ֥הּ תִּשָּֽׂא׃

records.literal_gloss: And if ever it is eaten any of the meat of the sacrifice of his peace offerings on the third day, not will be accepted the [one who] presented it; not it will be reckoned to him; foul meat it will be, and the person [who] eats of it its iniquity will bear.

en.L: And if any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings is indeed eaten on the third day, the one who brought it near will not be accepted; it will not be counted to him; it will be foul [meat], and the person who eats of it will bear the iniquity.
en.B: Should any meat of the peace offering be eaten on the third day, the one who brought it will not be accepted, and the offering will not count in their favor. It is foul meat, and whoever eats any of it will bear the guilt.
en.R: If any meat from the peace offering is eaten on the third day, the person who brought the offering will not be accepted. The offering will do them no good. That meat has gone bad. Anyone who eats it will have to suffer for their sin.

decisions.choice: not accepted, not reckoned to him: the whole offering loses its value
decisions.reason: To be "accepted" is the purpose of every offering (1:3-4). Eating the meat too late undoes that: the offering is not credited to the worshiper. The same words are used of the sacrifice in 19:7.

decisions.choice: foul meat: spoiled sacrificial meat
decisions.reason: The word is used only of sacrificial meat kept too long (19:7) or of unclean food (Ezekiel 4:14; Isaiah 65:4). It means a disgusting thing, unfit for God and for people.

decisions.choice: bear its iniquity: be held guilty and liable to punishment
decisions.reason: To bear iniquity is to carry the guilt of a wrong and its consequences (5:1, 17). The one who eats, not only the one who offered, is held guilty.

decisions.choice: the iniquity
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "her iniquity", the pronoun agreeing with the feminine word for "person". Literal says "the iniquity" so as not to suggest that a woman is meant; compare 17:10.

decisions.choice: That meat has gone bad; will have to suffer for their sin
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "foul" and "bear the iniquity" mean.

source.text: וְהַבָּשָׂ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּ֤ע בְּכָל־טָמֵא֙ לֹ֣א יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל בָּאֵ֖שׁ יִשָּׂרֵ֑ף וְהַ֨בָּשָׂ֔ר כָּל־טָה֖וֹר יֹאכַ֥ל בָּשָֽׂר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the meat which touches any unclean [thing] not will be eaten; with fire it will be burned; and the meat, every clean [person] will eat meat.

en.L: And the flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. And [as for] the flesh, everyone who is clean may eat [the] flesh.
en.B: If the meat comes into contact with anything unclean, no one may eat it; it must be burned in the fire. Otherwise, the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean.
en.R: If the meat touches anything unclean, it must not be eaten. It must be burned up. Anyone who is clean may eat the rest of the meat.

decisions.choice: unclean ... clean: fit or unfit for contact with holy things
decisions.reason: Being unclean is a state that bars a person or thing from what is holy, caused by contact with death, certain animals, discharges and the like (5:2; 11:4; chapters 12-15). The meat of the peace offering is holy, so it must not touch anything unclean, and only clean people may eat it (verses 20-21).

decisions.choice: and the meat, every clean one will eat meat: anyone clean may eat it
decisions.reason: The verse first names the subject, "the meat", and then says what may be done with it. Unlike the most holy offerings (6:22; 7:6), the peace offering may be eaten by anyone who is clean, not only by priests.

decisions.choice: [as for]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "as for" to show that "the flesh" is set at the head of the sentence as its topic.

source.text: וְהַנֶּ֜פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאכַ֣ל בָּשָׂ֗ר מִזֶּ֤בַח הַשְּׁלָמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַיהוָ֔ה וְטֻמְאָת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the person who eats meat from the sacrifice of the peace offerings which [belongs] to Yahweh, and his uncleanness [is] on him, and will be cut off that person from his kin.

en.L: But the person who eats flesh from the sacrifice of peace offerings that [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while his uncleanness [is] on him, that person shall be cut off from his people.
en.B: If anyone who is unclean eats meat from a peace offering that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that person must be cut off from the people.
en.R: Suppose someone is unclean and eats meat from a peace offering that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That person must be removed from the people.

decisions.choice: that person will be cut off from his people: lose his place among God's people
decisions.reason: This is the gravest penalty in the laws of Leviticus, used for wrongs against what is holy and against the covenant: eating sacred meat while unclean (verses 20-21), eating the fat of offerings (verse 25) or blood (verse 27; 17:10, 14), working on the Day of Atonement (23:29-30), and sexual sins (18:29). The passive does not say who acts. In 17:10 and 20:3-6 God says "I will cut him off", so the penalty is often God's own act rather than a sentence carried out by the community; 20:2-3 sets the two side by side, stoning by the people and cutting off by God. What it means in practice is not stated. It may mean early death, the end of the person's family line, or being cut off from one's ancestors after death, in contrast with being "gathered to one's people" (Genesis 25:8). Exile from the community is another reading. All agree that the person loses their place in Israel.

decisions.choice: which belongs to Yahweh while unclean: holy food must not meet uncleanness
decisions.reason: The peace offering is the LORD's, so eating it is sharing in a holy meal. Uncleanness and holiness must be kept apart (verse 19; 22:3-7).

decisions.choice: cut off from his people (Literal); cut off from the people (Balanced); removed from the people (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "from her people", the pronoun agreeing with the feminine word for "person". Literal says "his" for the person; Balanced and Readable say "the people", as in 17:10. Readable says "removed" so that "cut off" is not taken as a bodily wound. "Must" marks a penalty, not a forecast.

source.text: וְנֶ֜פֶשׁ כִּֽי־תִגַּ֣ע בְּכָל־טָמֵ֗א בְּטֻמְאַ֤ת אָדָם֙ א֣וֹ׀בִּבְהֵמָ֣ה טְמֵאָ֗ה א֚וֹ בְּכָל־שֶׁ֣קֶץ טָמֵ֔א וְאָכַ֛ל מִבְּשַׂר־זֶ֥בַח הַשְּׁלָמִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַיהוָ֑ה וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּֽיהָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And a person when it touches any unclean [thing], the uncleanness of humankind or livestock unclean or any detestable thing unclean, and eats of the meat of the sacrifice of the peace offerings which [belongs] to Yahweh, and will be cut off that person from his kin.

en.L: And a person who touches anything unclean, the uncleanness of a human or an unclean animal or any unclean detestable thing, and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings that [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that person shall be cut off from his people.'"
en.B: If a person has touched anything unclean, such as human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or some unclean detestable creature, and then eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that person must be cut off from the people.'"
en.R: Someone might touch something unclean. It might be an unclean person, an unclean animal, or some disgusting unclean creature. If that person then eats meat from a peace offering that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that person must be removed from the people.'"

decisions.choice: the uncleanness of a human: uncleanness that comes from a person
decisions.reason: This means the uncleanness of a human body, such as a discharge, childbirth, skin disease or a corpse (chapters 12-15; Numbers 19:11-16). Whoever touches it is unclean in turn (5:3).

decisions.choice: detestable thing: some Hebrew manuscripts read "swarming thing"
decisions.reason: The Westminster Leningrad Codex reads "detestable thing", the word used for unclean water creatures and insects in 11:10-23. Some Hebrew manuscripts, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Syriac read a word that differs by one letter, "swarming thing", as in the parallel 5:2 and 22:5. The sense is nearly the same: small unclean creatures. This translation follows the Codex.

decisions.choice: the speech closes
decisions.reason: This verse ends the instructions to Aaron and his sons that began at 6:18. A new speech, to all the people, begins at verse 22.

decisions.choice: disgusting
decisions.reason: Readable says "disgusting" for this word, as in chapter 11.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a new speech: fat and blood are not to be eaten
decisions.reason: This speech (verses 23-27) is for all the people, not only the priests. It repeats and explains the rule of 3:17.

source.text: דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּל־חֵ֜לֶב שׁ֥וֹר וְכֶ֛שֶׂב וָעֵ֖ז לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to the people of Israel, saying, any fat of an ox and a young ram and a goat not you must eat.

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'Any fat of ox or sheep or goat you shall not eat.
en.B: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'You must not eat any fat from cattle, sheep or goats.
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'You must not eat the fat of any cow, sheep or goat.

decisions.choice: fat: the fat parts that are burned on the altar
decisions.reason: The word means the layers of fat around the inner organs and the kidneys, and the sheep's fat tail, which are the LORD's portion (3:3-4, 9-10, 16). It does not mean the fat that runs through the meat.

decisions.choice: ox, sheep, goat: the animals offered in sacrifice
decisions.reason: These are the three kinds of animal brought as peace offerings (3:1, 7, 12). Verse 25 gives the reason the rule applies to them.

decisions.choice: cattle (Balanced); cow (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means one head of cattle, male or female. Literal keeps "ox".

source.text: וְחֵ֤לֶב נְבֵלָה֙ וְחֵ֣לֶב טְרֵפָ֔ה יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה לְכָל־מְלָאכָ֑ה וְאָכֹ֖ל לֹ֥א תֹאכְלֻֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a torn animal may be used for any work, but certainly not you must eat it.

en.L: And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a torn [animal] may be used for any work, but you shall certainly not eat it.
en.B: The fat of an animal that died on its own, or that was torn apart by wild animals, can be put to any use, but you must on no account eat it.
en.R: If an animal dies by itself or is killed by wild animals, you may use its fat for other things. But you must never eat it.

decisions.choice: a carcass, a torn animal: animals that died without being slaughtered
decisions.reason: A carcass is an animal that died of itself; a torn animal is one killed by a wild beast. Their meat must not be eaten (17:15; 22:8; Exodus 22:31), and touching a carcass makes a person unclean (11:39-40).

decisions.choice: certainly not eat: an emphatic prohibition
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. The fat may be used, for example for lamps or leather, but never eaten.

source.text: כִּ֚י כָּל־אֹכֵ֣ל חֵ֔לֶב מִן־הַ֨בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֥יב מִמֶּ֛נָּה אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הָאֹכֶ֖לֶת מֵֽעַמֶּֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For any [one who] eats fat from the animal which he will present from it a fire offering to Yahweh, and will be cut off the person [who] eats from his kin.

en.L: For anyone who eats fat from the animal from which one brings near an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the person who eats shall be cut off from his people.
en.B: If anyone eats fat from an animal of the kind presented to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a food offering, the one who eats it must be cut off from the people.
en.R: Anyone who eats the fat of an animal that could be offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a food offering must be removed from the people.

decisions.choice: the animal from which one presents: an animal of a kind used in offerings
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means any animal of the kinds offered (verse 23), whether or not that animal was itself sacrificed. It could also mean only the animal actually brought as an offering, but verse 24 forbids the fat even of animals that died unslaughtered.

decisions.choice: cut off from his people: as in verse 20
decisions.reason: See the note on verse 20.

source.text: וְכָל־דָּם֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכְל֔וּ בְּכֹ֖ל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶ֑ם לָע֖וֹף וְלַבְּהֵמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And any blood not you must eat in all your dwelling places, of birds and of livestock.

en.L: And any blood you shall not eat in all your dwellings, of bird or of beast.
en.B: You must not eat any blood at all, whether from a bird or from an animal, wherever you live.
en.R: Wherever you live, never eat blood, from a bird or from any other animal.

decisions.choice: any blood you shall not eat: the rule of 3:17 and 17:10-14
decisions.reason: Eating blood was forbidden from the time of Noah (Genesis 9:4). Chapter 17 explains why: the life is in the blood, and God has given it to make atonement on the altar (17:11).

decisions.choice: in all your dwellings: wherever you live
decisions.reason: As in 3:17, the rule holds everywhere, not only at the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: beast: any land animal
decisions.reason: Unlike the fat (verse 23), the rule on blood covers every bird and animal, wild game as well (17:13).

source.text: כָּל־נֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאכַ֣ל כָּל־דָּ֑ם וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵֽעַמֶּֽיהָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Every person who eats any blood, and will be cut off that person from his kin.

en.L: Any person who eats any blood, that person shall be cut off from his people.'"
en.B: Whoever eats any blood, that person must be cut off from the people.'"
en.R: Anyone who eats any blood must be removed from the people.'"

decisions.choice: cut off from his people: as in verse 20
decisions.reason: In 17:10 God says he himself will act against the one who eats blood.

decisions.choice: the speech closes
decisions.reason: The speech of verse 22 ends here. Another, about the priests' share of the peace offering, begins at verse 28.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a new speech: the priests' share of the peace offering
decisions.reason: This last speech of the section (verses 29-34) tells the people what part of their peace offerings goes to the priests.

source.text: דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הַמַּקְרִ֞יב אֶת־זֶ֤בַח שְׁלָמָיו֙ לַיהוָ֔ה יָבִ֧יא אֶת־קָרְבָּנ֛וֹ לַיהוָ֖ה מִזֶּ֥בַח שְׁלָמָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to the people of Israel, saying, the [one who] presents the sacrifice of his peace offerings to Yahweh will bring his present to Yahweh from the sacrifice of his peace offerings.

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'The one who brings near the sacrifice of his peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shall bring his offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the sacrifice of his peace offerings.
en.B: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When anyone offers a peace offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they themselves must bring from it a gift for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'When you bring a peace offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you must bring part of it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} yourself as a gift.

decisions.choice: will bring his offering from the sacrifice: the worshiper brings the LORD's portion himself
decisions.reason: The "offering" taken from the peace offering is the part that goes to God and his priests: the fat and the breast (verse 30). The worshiper is to bring it in person, as verse 30 says: "his own hands".

decisions.choice: offering: as in 1:2
decisions.reason: The general word for what is brought near to God.

decisions.choice: anyone ... they themselves (Balanced); you ... yourself (Readable)
decisions.reason: The worshiper may be a man or a woman. Balanced uses "anyone" and "they"; Readable speaks to the reader, as in 1:2. "Themselves" and "yourself" anticipate "his own hands" in verse 30.

source.text: יָדָ֣יו תְּבִיאֶ֔ינָה אֵ֖ת אִשֵּׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֶת־הַחֵ֤לֶב עַל־הֶֽחָזֶה֙ יְבִיאֶ֔נּוּ אֵ֣ת הֶחָזֶ֗ה לְהָנִ֥יף אֹת֛וֹ תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: His own hands will bring the fire offerings of Yahweh: the fat with the breast he will bring it, the breast to wave it [as] a wave offering before Yahweh.

en.L: His own hands shall bring the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: the fat with the breast he shall bring, the breast to wave it [as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The worshiper must carry {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s food offerings in their own hands: the fat, together with the breast. The breast is for waving before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering.
en.R: You must carry the food offerings for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in your own hands. Bring the fat along with the breast. The breast must be waved before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering.

decisions.choice: to wave it as a wave offering: to present it to God by a motion before the altar
decisions.reason: The verb means to move something to and fro, or to swing or raise it. The breast is held out before the LORD and so given to him, and he then gives it to the priests (verse 34). The rite is shown in 8:27-29 and 9:21, and the same word is used of the Levites given to God's service (Numbers 8:11-21) and of gold and bronze given for the tabernacle (Exodus 35:22; 38:24), which cannot have been waved. So the word may name a ritual act of presenting rather than a waving motion, and some understand it as an "elevation offering", lifted up before God. The breast of the wave offering always belongs to the priests (10:14-15; Numbers 18:18).

decisions.choice: his own hands: the worshiper, not the priest, brings these parts
decisions.reason: The one who offers carries the LORD's portion to the altar himself. At the ordination the parts were put into the priests' hands in the same way (8:27).

decisions.choice: the fire offerings of Yahweh: as in 1:9
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means the fat for the altar together with the breast, which is presented before God but not burned.

decisions.choice: The worshiper ... their own hands (Balanced); your own hands (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, Balanced names the worshiper and Readable speaks to the reader. Literal keeps "his".

source.text: וְהִקְטִ֧יר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־הַחֵ֖לֶב הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וְהָיָה֙ הֶֽחָזֶ֔ה לְאַהֲרֹ֖ן וּלְבָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And the priest will make smoke the fat on the altar, and will belong the breast to Aaron and to his sons.

en.L: And the priest shall make the fat smoke on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and to his sons.
en.B: The fat the priest is to turn into smoke on the altar; the breast goes to Aaron and his sons.
en.R: The priest must burn the fat on the altar. The breast is for Aaron and his sons.

decisions.choice: the breast to Aaron and his sons: to the priests as a body
decisions.reason: The breast is shared among all the priests, while the right thigh goes to the officiating priest alone (verse 33).

source.text: וְאֵת֙ שׁ֣וֹק הַיָּמִ֔ין תִּתְּנ֥וּ תְרוּמָ֖ה לַכֹּהֵ֑ן מִזִּבְחֵ֖י שַׁלְמֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the thigh of the right you will give [as] a contribution to the priest from the sacrifices of your peace offerings.

en.L: And the right thigh you shall give [as] a contribution to the priest from the sacrifices of your peace offerings.
en.B: From your peace offerings you must also hand over the right thigh as a contribution for the priest.
en.R: You must also give the priest the right thigh from your peace offerings. It is a gift set apart for him.

decisions.choice: a contribution: a portion taken off and set apart for God and his priests
decisions.reason: The noun comes from a verb meaning to lift or take off. It names a part removed from a larger whole and handed over to God, who gives it to the priests: here the thigh, elsewhere a loaf (7:14), materials for the tabernacle (Exodus 25:2-3), or a share of the harvest and of tithes (Numbers 15:19-21; 18:8, 11, 26). It does not describe a lifting rite, as the older rendering "heave offering" suggested; the thigh is not said to be waved here, though in 10:15 it is brought with the breast for waving.

decisions.choice: the right thigh: the upper part of the hind leg
decisions.reason: The thigh was a choice cut of meat. When Samuel honored Saul he set before him the thigh (1 Samuel 9:23-24). The right side was the side of honor.

decisions.choice: a gift set apart for him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "contribution" by what it is, as in 7:14 and 10:14.

source.text: הַמַּקְרִ֞יב אֶת־דַּ֧ם הַשְּׁלָמִ֛ים וְאֶת־הַחֵ֖לֶב מִבְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֑ן ל֧וֹ תִהְיֶ֛ה שׁ֥וֹק הַיָּמִ֖ין לְמָנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The [one who] presents the blood of the peace offerings and the fat from the sons of Aaron, to him will belong the thigh of the right as a portion.

en.L: The one among the sons of Aaron who brings near the blood of the peace offerings and the fat, to him the right thigh shall belong as a portion.
en.B: That thigh is the share of whichever of Aaron's sons offers the blood and the fat of the peace offering.
en.R: The right thigh is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the peace offering. It is his share.

decisions.choice: the one among the sons of Aaron who presents: the officiating priest
decisions.reason: The priest who performs the altar rite for that offering receives the thigh, just as he receives the bread (verse 14).

decisions.choice: a portion: an allotted share
decisions.reason: The word is used for a share of food given to someone (8:29; 1 Samuel 1:4-5).

decisions.choice: the priest
decisions.reason: Readable says "the priest" for "the one among the sons of Aaron".

source.text: כִּי֩ אֶת־חֲזֵ֨ה הַתְּנוּפָ֜ה וְאֵ֣ת׀שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֗ה לָקַ֨חְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִזִּבְחֵ֖י שַׁלְמֵיהֶ֑ם וָאֶתֵּ֣ן אֹ֠תָם לְאַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֵ֤ן וּלְבָנָיו֙ לְחָק־עוֹלָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: For the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution I have taken from the people of Israel from the sacrifices of their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a prescribed portion of perpetuity from the people of Israel.

en.L: For the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution I have taken from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the sacrifices of their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a due forever from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.'"
en.B: For I have taken the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from the peace offerings of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as their permanent share from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.'"
en.R: I have taken two parts from the peace offerings of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: the breast that was waved before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and the thigh that was set apart. I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons. They will be their share from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} for all time.'"

decisions.choice: I have taken ... I have given: the portions pass through God's hands to the priests
decisions.reason: The breast and thigh are first God's, taken by him from the people's offerings, and only then the priests'. The priests live from what is given to God (Numbers 18:8-11; Deuteronomy 18:1-3).

decisions.choice: a due forever: a lasting right
decisions.reason: The word means an allotted share fixed by rule (10:13-15); with "forever" it is a right that does not lapse.

decisions.choice: the speech closes
decisions.reason: God speaks in the first person here ("I have taken"). Verses 35-36 speak of the LORD in the third person and sum up what has been said, so the speech that began at verse 29 ends with this verse.

decisions.choice: that was waved before me
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the wave offering" by what was done with the breast (verse 30). The pronoun is God's, as the speaker.

source.text: זֹ֣את מִשְׁחַ֤ת אַהֲרֹן֙ וּמִשְׁחַ֣ת בָּנָ֔יו מֵאִשֵּׁ֖י יְהוָ֑ה בְּיוֹם֙ הִקְרִ֣יב אֹתָ֔ם לְכַהֵ֖ן לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the share of Aaron and the share of his sons from the fire offerings of Yahweh on [the] day [when] he presented them to serve as priests to Yahweh,

en.L: This [is] the portion of Aaron and the portion of his sons from the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, on the day he brought them near to serve as priests to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: This is the share of Aaron and his sons from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s food offerings, from the day they were presented to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as priests,
en.R: This was the share for Aaron and his sons from the food offerings burned on the altar for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It was theirs from the day they were brought forward to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as priests.

decisions.choice: the portion: the share assigned to the priests, perhaps "the anointed portion"
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "anoint" (verse 36), and may mean the share that goes with the priests' anointing. A similar word is used of the priests' share in Numbers 18:8, where it is often taken to mean "a portion" or "a measure". Either way it names what is due to them.

decisions.choice: on the day he presented them: Moses, at the ordination
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward when they were ordained (8:6, 13, 24; Exodus 29:4, 8), so he is most likely meant; the sense is the same if it is read "on the day they were presented".

decisions.choice: this: a summary in narrative
decisions.reason: After the speech closes (verse 34), verses 35-38 sum up the rules of 6:1-7:34.

decisions.choice: they were presented (Balanced); they were brought forward (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive, since the subject is not named.

source.text: אֲשֶׁר֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ מָשְׁח֣וֹ אֹתָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: which commanded Yahweh to give to them on the day he anointed them from the people of Israel, a prescribed portion of perpetuity for their generations.

en.L: which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded to give to them, on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} anointed them, from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, a statute forever for their generations.
en.B: which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to give them on the day they were anointed. It is a permanent rule for all their generations.
en.R: On the day they were anointed, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to give them this share. It is a rule for all time, for every generation to come.

decisions.choice: on the day he anointed them: Yahweh, who anointed them through Moses
decisions.reason: The nearest subject is Yahweh, who commanded the anointing (Exodus 28:41; 40:13-15); Moses carried it out (8:12, 30). The phrase may also be read impersonally, "on the day they were anointed". The anointing set them apart as priests, and their share dates from it.

decisions.choice: a statute forever for their generations: as in 3:17
decisions.reason: The priests' right to these portions lasts for all their descendants. The word is the one for a fixed share in verse 34, here meaning the rule that grants it.

decisions.choice: they were anointed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive, because the one who performed the anointing was Moses, acting for the LORD.

decisions.choice: for every generation to come
decisions.reason: Readable joins "forever" and "for their generations" without repeating "for all time".

source.text: זֹ֣את הַתּוֹרָ֗ה לָֽעֹלָה֙ לַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְלַֽחַטָּ֖את וְלָאָשָׁ֑ם וְלַ֨מִּלּוּאִ֔ים וּלְזֶ֖בַח הַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the law for the burnt offering, for the grain offering, and for the sin offering, and for the guilt offering, and for the ordination offerings, and for the sacrifice of the peace offerings,

en.L: This [is] the law for the burnt offering, for the grain offering, and for the sin offering, and for the guilt offering, and for the ordination [offerings], and for the sacrifice of peace offerings,
en.B: These are the instructions for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering and the peace offering,
en.R: These are the rules for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the offering for ordaining priests, and the peace offering.

decisions.choice: this is the law: the closing summary of the offering laws
decisions.reason: The verse names each offering whose rules were given in 6:1-7:36, in the order of the instructions to the priests.

decisions.choice: the ordination offerings: the offerings that install the priests
decisions.reason: The word means "fillings", from the idiom "fill the hand", to install as priest (see 8:22, 28, 33). The grain offering of 6:13-16, offered "on the day he is anointed", belongs to the ordination; the rite itself was commanded in Exodus 29 and is carried out in chapter 8.

decisions.choice: the offering for ordaining priests
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ordination" as 8:22 does.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּהַ֣ר סִינָ֑י בְּי֨וֹם צַוֺּת֜וֹ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַקְרִ֧יב אֶת־קָרְבְּנֵיהֶ֛ם לַיהוָ֖ה בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: which commanded Yahweh Moses on [the] mountain of Sinai on [the] day he commanded the people of Israel to present their presents to Yahweh in the wilderness of Sinai.

en.L: which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel to bring near their offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in the wilderness of Sinai.
en.B: which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses on Mount Sinai at the time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, in the wilderness of Sinai, to bring their offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave these rules to Moses on Mount Sinai. That was in the Sinai Desert, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to bring their offerings to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: on Mount Sinai ... in the wilderness of Sinai: at Sinai, during the stay there
decisions.reason: The laws were given from the tent of meeting (1:1), which stood at the foot of the mountain. "On Mount Sinai" may mean "at Mount Sinai", as the same words are used in 25:1, 26:46 and 27:34; the wilderness of Sinai is the region around it (Exodus 19:1-2).

decisions.choice: on the day: at the time
decisions.reason: "On the day" here means "when", as in Genesis 2:4, not one particular day.

decisions.choice: the Sinai Desert
decisions.reason: Readable says "desert" for "wilderness", the dry land around Sinai.

decisions.choice: The LORD gave these rules to Moses
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and names the rules of verse 37 as the subject.
